comment:
This trail has many many rocks 
Good hiking footwear is a must 
Well worth the effort 
Fantastic views
Know that the rocks can get a little slippery but as a non-hiker with running shoes, I still found it very doable!
Tough hike, but worth it!  Wear hiking boots.
Loved the view! Clearly marked trail. We saw a bear towards the end of the hike by the parking lot. Just a heads up!
Very beautiful view once you reach the top, however can be hard on the knees and feet if you are not used to hiking
Good and easy hike! Rainy condition makes it slippery, have fun!
Park a km before the start of trail outaide school.
A lovely trail, can be a little crowded in places. Be careful with your footing as the ground is very uneven throughout
Lots more exposed roots and rocks than I thought. Saw some families but if you have joint problems it may prove to be a bit difficult and would advise otherwise.
Need to pay for parking before arriving
Noice to have Robert with me for this one.
Great trail with beautiful lookouts at the end! Most of the trail is uneven rocks and tree roots so proper footwear is recommended! You also need a parking permit in the summer/early fall.

Technical trail with many rocks, roots, and small boulders to navigate makes for fancy foot work and balance challenges. Proper footwear, water and a snack to munch on at the top. Parking available at nearby school if lot is full or paid street parking about 10 mins away. Busy at Lookout point. Great workout, enjoy your hike replete with mossy beds and lovely light draping the birch trees.
Good view, the road is kind of hard to walk
AMAZING VIEWS + had to run back to my car
Beautiful views for a hike that is not too challenging, but definately you need proper shoes due to all the roots and rocks. Not too busy at 8am start with only 3 cars in the parking lot.
Beautiful views at the Lions Head lookout. Took us about 2.5 hours with time to take photos and enjoy the views. Clearly marked through a forested area. Very rocky - moderate hike.
Beautiful woodland walk with breathtaking views of Georgian Bay.
It took us 4 hour to finish moderate hike
Great hike to strengthen the ankles  🙌
Did trail Monday July 13th, great views, look for trail markings on trees. Need parking pass. Started at 430pm. Saw bear abt half mile from trailhead.
Really nice view points! Easy to moderate. Rewarding and accessible.

black bear sighting in previous weeks, snakes as well.

trail is rocky for the first half and muddy in small areas, also not super easy to follow tree blazes near the summit, but great views.

We went just after it had rained, too many bugs in the beginning, dress accordingly .
Insanely great views

Great trail, with the great view at the end. It takes a bit longer than advertised. Where in relatively good shape, but took it slow as it had just rain and the rocks were a little slippery, and it took us about three hours and 15 minutes there and back with lots of time at the lookout.
Rocks are slippery, uneven ground but very easy walking and beautiful views
Amazing
Great trail, just very rocky
Buy a parking pass
Make a parking reservation!!
Very uneven trail ....very crowded...tobermory trails much better

Solid hike! Lots of tree branches and rocks on the floor but was doable. I went mid May and the temperature was great. I would say this hike gets moderate near the lookout, otherwise it’s an easy trail.
Great
Definitely a difficult path but worth the view
SUPER ROCKY! but beautiful
If you love rockless slopes don’t come. If you have short legs don’t come. If you have height fright don’t come. Otherwise 10/10 recommend.
Lots of wildflowers blooming in late May.
Great trail, mostly rocky terrain so good footwear is necessary. Beautiful views!
Very busy today and slippery conditions after last nights heavy rain.
Beautiful. Come early and bring lots of water. Wear hiking boots or shoes.
Extremely rocky and very hard to walk in and manoeuvre over the rocks.
Amazing views.  It’s worth the hike.  Probably best in dry weather.  Lots of rocks.
Sensible footwear needed as some scrambling over rocks. Beautiful views over the bay
A bit muddy and ticks are out but otherwise great trail.
Lovely & somewhat challenging hike to the lookout. Currently still a bit snowy & icy as of the beginning of April 2026, so make sure to wear good shoes & bring/wear necessary gear.
Parking was free this time, there’s paid parking around peak season. Trail got slippery and icy closer to the look outs, make sure you have good shoes. Views were gorgeous! :]
Beautiful as always. Use caution as it’s icy beneath the snow!

Excellent trail, great conditions, great views. Winter has not yet arrived so all you need are your hiking boots for the rugged conditions. There are a few easily avoidable muddy spots at the start of the forest. Parking off season is free, and it's less busy as well.
Beautiful trail with so many lookout view points.
Super great trail! The birch trees were amazing in the fall! Would definitely recommend. Lots of great view points!
Does not live up to the hype and fanfare around this hike. But adequate if you want to spend a couple of hours in the woods.
Need to pre-book for parking
Nature was very interesting. Only an outhouse at entrance and limited parking, so prepare accordingly. Rather busy on long weekend. Remember to pack out!
Rocky but not that much that it’s difficult for someone experience, not much elevation so shouldn’t be too difficult, can be slippery and crowded however

There is rocky, uneven terrain for most of the hike. Lots of viewpoints along the escarpment. The last cliff is a larger area with 180 degree views of the water and the escarpment. The Lions Head cliff is quite dangerous so I wouldn’t recommend bringing children, unless they fully understand the situation. I brought my 2 puppies for the entire hike and they did just fine (probably even better than I did).
Little longer of a trail but is a beautiful hike with lots of rocky paths, great Clift views a little over halfway through. Definitely worth the view.
Unsteady under foot for a good bit of the trail.

Great long 8km trail in and out. Is it worth it ?  YESSS!!! For the views. Is it exhausting….yes lol. It’s quite the long hike but there are things along the way to see and very nice views as you hike further. No bathrooms along the way only in the parking lot. !!! Bring water and snacks

My favourite hike in the bruce pen area. We found it to be just the right amount of challenging, a bit of rock clambering needed, with a breathtaking view to finish. A little bit confusing as to how far is left to go, as the trail signs pointing you onward have no distance written. There are lots of mini lookouts along the way, we often stopped thinking is this lions head? And saw other people doing the same. There is a RED OUTLINED Lion’s Head Lookout sign at the final lookout, so keep going! It’s worth the trek if you are able. Bring lots of water and snacks, we ended up spending 4 hours here. Dogs are allowed but will need very good stamina and climbing abilities. Our malinois had tons of fun. Be careful with kids/dogs towards the end as there is a sudden crevasse you will need to pass over. But it means you made it. Have fun!

Stunning view! The weather was pretty warm and dry when we went, but some of the forested areas were still muddy and the rocks were slippery when wet, so keep that in mind if you’re going in wetter conditions. The terrain is pretty bumpy but the elevation isn’t too bad. Either way, I recommend bringing proper footwear with good grip (i.e. trail runners or hiking boots). It’s a beautiful hike, truly a gem in Ontario’s nature
Best to go nice and early
I would label this an aggressive moderate trail. We were able to do it with a 15 month on our backs. But it definitely had some challenges! Lookout is a bit confusing but super beautiful.
Good easy trail!
Take your time. You must look down almost always. Stop and enjoy the experience

Forest section isn’t the most interesting but is definitely peaceful. Very rocky so watch your step. Payoff cliff views up top make this one worth it though. Lots of stop points with stunning views along the way to the ending.

Great hike with several photo opportunities on the cliff side before the main event (actual lookout). Wear appropriate footwear as some sections can be a little bit challenging. Not crowded in the early morning; porta potties available at trailhead; recommend to reserve parking ahead of time—they’ll send reminder texts FYI.
Very nice Lookout view but to reach it have to hike a hard hiking trail with rocks and big trees.
Fantastic hike with amazing views! Definitely a slight challenge at times but well worth it
Trail with a lot of rocks on the way with elevation. Don't be tricked by the short distance. It's definitely a difficult level trail. But view is absolutely stunning and it is a interesting trail.
Well worn

Get there early and pre pay for parking. Small parking lot was full. You can park about a km away at a school and walk to the trail.  There is a shuttle if you ware there on weekends after 10am.

Very busy trail but if you get there early you miss the rush.

Also very rocky so be prepared to roll your ankles even if you have good boots.

Definitely do recommend this trail. Difficult but rewarding.

All the way to the lookout by the forest, the forest is not so interesting. Lookout is really good, but crowded. Little Cove trail is much interesting: the forest, the beach on the begin of the path (but was crowded after 9 am!), etc.

I did this trail with my partner today. It took us about 1.5 hours each way walking at a very brisk pace. We were passing quite a few people along the way. There are no bathrooms anywhere which is something to keep in mind. The terrain was quite difficult, rocky and had lots of tree roots sticking up through the ground. My apple watch tracked the hike as 4.5 km each way though. So be sure to bring good hiking shoes and lots of water and snacks to keep you going. I definitely would say this trail is hard, not moderate so be prepared to sweat haha once we reached the lookout the views were absolutely incredible!
Fanstastic views
First hike! Good views!
Trail is long but fun. Definitely try it once!
Rocky trail to start. All shaded. Beautiful views of the lake!

Wonderful view from the look out! Worth the effort of getting there. 
The trail is well marked but some parts are very rocky which makes it difficult to walk.

Fantastic amazing spectacular views. I did a four hour parking permit. I think it was $20. From that parking to the views I would say it was about 45 minutes. Pretty treacherous terrain but manageable, saw as young as two years old to grandma‘s on the trail. But I would base your parking off of how long you want to spend on the views because four hours was quite a turnaround and I’m pretty agile on the trails. A note take a garbage bag with you because there are despicable human beings who just leaves their trash on the trail as you will see in my last photo.

Beautiful view points and lots of variety in the terrain. The blazes are visible and frequent, which made trail navigation easy. There’s a variety of terrains but it is quite rocky so I would definitely recommend sturdy shoes and would probably advise against bringing dogs that aren’t used to hiking. Highly recommend going early in the day as we saw very few people when going up around 9 am but a ton on the way back down at around 10:30 onwards. Very vigilant parking attendants so make sure to reserve your parking online and stick to your time slot if using the trailhead parking lot or park by the overflow lot at the arena.
Great trail, awesome view points.
Longer than it looks, proper footwear recommended, especially if it has rained. Beautiful view points, easy to find trail markers.
I only made it to the lakeside viewing platform — it was so beautiful, totally worth it.

Due to its popularity, the Lion's Head area can get very crowded, particularly on summer weekends. Arriving early is essential to secure parking, which often requires a pre-booked reservation and a fee during the busy season. The spring and fall offer a great alternative, with comfortable temperatures and fewer crowds. Overall, the Lion's Head Lookout Trail is a fantastic hike that showcases some of Ontario's most beautiful natural scenery and is a must-do for any avid hiker.
Beautiful trail! Have strong ankles for this one cause it’s super rocky, but so worth the trek!
Careful not to slip on rocks when wet :)
Trail is definately hard however amazing views

Stimulating, rocky trail with no dull sections at all. Gorgeous viewpoints are scattered throughout the 2nd half of the trail. Make sure to go just past the lookout to see the "donut" island. Only downside is parking; you must reserve it online and it was already full before 10am on a Wednesday -- park for free at the school or arena instead.
Book parking in advance, phenomenal trail and directions throughout
Great trail. Good challenge
Nice hike to the lookout and back. Trail was good, very rocky and lots of roots (standard Bruce Trail). Not a hike for beginners.
Very busy trail. Extremely bumpy rocks for the majority of the way. Definitely moderate.
Early to bed, early to rise makes a man healthy wealthy and wise!
Awesome trail, challenging since there is a lot of rocks but easy enough, the view is worth it trust me. Went really early to watch the sunrise, loved it
Beautiful trail with good views. Takes 3-4 hrs for newbies out and back

Probably the best hike I’ve done in Ontario. This is a perfect hike for beginners who are looking for a tiny bit of a challenge. Lots of family’s and people of all ages on the trail which was amazing! The view at the very end is worth all of it! Definitely pack a lunch to enjoy it at the very end! 

I did bring bear spray due to the recent bear sightings in the area but luckily didn’t have to use it! 10/10 recommend

I definitely recommend good hiking shoes for this trail though. There are muddy areas and tons of slippery stones.

Fantastic 180 degree view at the Lookout. There are also other views of the water along the way. Takes about 1.5-2 hours each way, depending how fast you walk. Trail was dry, moderate amount of mosquitos. There are lots of trees that provide shade the entire way. Lots of medium sized rocks and tree roots the climb over, a short rock climb is needed to get to the top of the lookout. Port a potties at the trailhead.
Beautiful trail- Need proper hiking shoes, lots of water… the BEST view point
Wear hiking foot wear!
Warm day. Bring extra water

Definitely a moderate trail with extremely beautiful views. I did see a black bear on the trail by the pothole. I tried to get a picture once I got a good distance away. I’m 330 lbs and did the trail in 5 hours, however I spent a lot of time at the different viewpoints
A tough trail with lots of rocks and roots to traverse. Rewarding views at the end of the trail
Remarkable views, well marked trails and a reasonable challenge.
Had such a good hike I recommend doing early morning it was so nice and no one was there.

It is one of the best trail I’ve been so far. The view is amazing through the trail. The trail is moderate difficulty. The whole trail is within the shades so you don’t feel the summer hotness as much as you do in your concrete room. So pull ur socks up and come to lions head ..

Very busy trail in the summer. Very rocky and took longer than anticipated. Beautiful views and would be great in the fall. It's kind of annoying that parking is only 4 hours but a lot of the trails take longer. Make sure you buy your parking well in advance.
Overrated
Easy trail with beautiful views, especially on sunny days. I didn't see any mosquitoes on this trail.
Absolutely beautiful trail with breathtaking overlooks.
Amazing lookout view
A bit crowded but beautiful day and beautiful views.

Be sure to wear proper footwear as the trail has greatly buried drain. There are sections where you will be moving over top of very uneven eroded limestone, and then onto flat well rod in earth and then undulating up and down with not just a lot of roots and rocks, but in some sections, you will have to hand hold on trees, etc. to get a good grip to climb. It depends how far along you go. You will know that you got to the lions head lookout as it does have a large white sign that says lions head lookout. But there are several lookout points before you get to that.
Great views, humid hike, not buggy. Rainforest vibes
Nice trail, average difficulty. Not many bugs.
Beautiful spot. Make you book parking in advance.
Beautiful trail with amazing cliff views! Trail is almost all escarpment rock so come with proper footwear
Beautiful as always! Make sure to book parking ahead of time!
Perfect place for sunrise
So relaxing!!
Beautiful views. Some muddy areas. Overall stunning hike.

More bugs flying than I would expect in May. 
The lookout point was a bit disappointing. No good view unless you risk your life walking out with lots of bugs flying.
Quite rocky but otherwise a great hike. Lovely views.

Great hike with best view at the end. The water is so clean and coloured. Totally worth it. Parking is on reservation basis so make sure to register your spot. If you miss the spot, you can park you car at Lion’s head town parking lot and walk extra 700 meters until the trail start point.
Eloped with Elopers & Co. @heyjeffmaeck @timothymuza @lcoulterphoto

I went in April last week around 4pm. There was no crowd at all. Parking still has some spots left. We got the Lion’s lookout completely for ourselves for 15-20 mins. :) round trip is around 7km which took us around 2 hours 50 mins. We went slow and steady with small breaks in between. Trail is beaten and lots of small trees hurdles, I did see couple of dogs on the way with people. Overall it’s a moderate to difficult for beginners. Don’t forget to wear shoes with proper padding as you will have to climb up and down the rocks. 100% recommended for a nice satisfying view. :) oh and there were no washrooms at all, may be because of the off-season.
Crowded trail. To be expected I suppose. Conditions were great.
Trails were packed down from use,  some slippery parts.  Fantastic views!

A bit harder than I expected, lots of incline/ decline and a bit of climbing towards the last km near the main lookout.
Good trail, no people out at all today (January)
Don't miss out just because it's winter!
Parts of trail are rocky. Boots are recommended. There is a bit of mud but easily avoidable. The views are gorgeous. Be sure to go down under the lookout to spot the lion’s head.
Great views. Wouldn’t recommend bringing young children or small dogs.

AWESOME Hike on the Bruce Trail!! Trail was busy with hikers enjoying the mild fall weather.
Stunning scenery! Challenging hike with crevices, roots & rocks and some elevation but the lookouts are  sooo worth it!
One of my top favourite hikes in Ontario.
Beautiful Fall hike! The trail was a bit rocky at some points but overall not too bad.
Bumpy and rocky but overall easy track
We just wanted to beat Jeff
Really rocky, lots of opportunities to stub your toes. Wear appropriate footwear. Involves a bit of uphill climbing but overall the view was worth it.
Was very long and tiring.
Fantastic. Better then expectations
Easy visible trail great view at the end!
Very rocky. Moderate to hard at times. Beautiful Views. Definitely worth it.
It was a moderate, rugged trail,but worth all difficulties, gorgeous views
It’s mostly a rocky trail. Beautiful views.
Rocky trail makes this a workout a bit. The views are most impressive once you make it to the Lion Head Rick and see the views from on top of it.  Trail is quite busy after 10 am
Gorgeous views. Lots of rocky paths so wear good hiking gear shoes!

Gorgeous view of Georgian Bay!

Difficulty: moderate
Roots and rocks
Good challenging trails.  Lots of rocky areas.  Nice view of the lookouts.

Terrible trail etiquette and obnoxious behaviour (yelling because you're taking photos, playing your music on a speaker, etc.). If you're looking for any semblance of peace and tranquility in nature, you're probably not going to get it by doing this trail. Slippery rocks. A bit muddy. The view was okay but one of the better ones in Ontario. Trekking poles may be helpful for some of the steeper sections.

Gorgeous trail, gorgeous lookout. The trail is very rugged; lots of slippery rock and roots. Good hiking boots are a MUST. I was shocked by the number of folks on this trail with basic runners on. I also recommend hiking early morning as it gets super busy around 10am. You just register for parking online; 4hr parking is $20, I think whole day is $30. 10/10 will be back to this trail again.
Lions head lookout has a stunning lookout. Very rugged terrain,  definitely need good footwear and hiking poles will really come in handy. Pack extra water.

Lots of boulders. Good shoes. Trecking  poles recommended. Note there is an emergency access road that is easy walking about 2.5 km in on the main trail from the Lions Head Provincial Reserve Parking (we took this road out and saved some more challenging g steps)
Nice easy trail, beautiful view points.
Amazing views

We hiked 11km, just under 3hrs.... it's a pretty easy hike just rocky which slows you down a bit... there's lots of look outs along the way which we stopped at each one too. Very pretty views and totally worth it. We went on a rainy day, so no issues with parking and the trail was very quiet
Dope trail
Rugged trail with moderate elevation gain.  Some steep inclines. Fabulous views from steep cliffs- no guard rails - caution needed.
Gorgeous views, terrain is very rocky the whole way - tough on ankles without a lot of flat terrain breaks. Eyes on your feet…

Free shuttle service that runs every half hour so you don’t have to park at the entrance which is $20.00 for 4 hours. 
Plan parking ahead of time to reserve it. Reception is terrible and made it very difficult to reserve a spot online which is required.

Yes it’s rocky but not so much that you have to rock climb. At most you might roll your ankles if you’re not careful because the ground is uneven. Don’t bring your grandparents here. Also clean up your garbage. Lots of of people dropping stuff including an entire bag of pretzels!
A bit slippery at the start today. Reserved the parking spot in advance.
Easy hike with well marked route. Beautiful view points on the way.

Make sure to bring extra water and to make a parking reservation. There is a shuttle service I would recommend earlier in the day but we went late and had to walk all the way back to the car as the bus stopped running by the time we were done. Rocks are hard to climb up and it’s a really long hike but it’s very beautiful

Probably about 3/4 of the trail is rocks and exposed root with some spots to climb almost 90 degrees up. Gorgeous views but you need good shoes and strong ankles and knees. Would definitely not call it moderate and would make sure your dog is ready to handle the conditions if you take them.
Great views. Rocky start.

This was my absolute favourite hike here! The hike was really pretty through the woods and took you to several beautiful lookouts. It was challenging enough and you’d definitely need proper hiking boots or running shoes for this. I would say you definitely have to be an experienced hiker for this and it isn’t just a leisurely hike. Trails are marked and easy to follow. There are lots of tree roots and rocks on the path at first, but wide enough trail that it made it fun. Then there are spots you need to climb up or down rocks near the look outs. It was a really fun and enjoyable hike! I wouldn’t recommend for children though, as it would be too challenging for them and unsafe. Bathrooms in parking  lot and you must reserve parking online. Great hike with lots of variety and nature! I’ve tried many here and this one’s my fav.
Great hike, just don't underestimate it. It starts easy and then it moves between medium and heavy medium throughout. 5 stars.
Amazing trail. Rocky surfaces definitely require attention but arnt super difficult. Great views!
The views are great!!!!

The Bruce Trail is very rugged and rocky, with lots of uneven limestone surfaces and quite a bit of mud after a stormy weekend. Crowded on a summer Monday afternoon; I had to park at the Lion's Head Arena because I didn't look for parking reservations until the night before. Reserve trailhead parking in advance! Most of the people here seemed to be Instagrammers, not serious hikers; many of them wore casual sneakers, and no one else was using poles (which I found quite helpful).
Rocky, some climbing, wear hiking shoes
Great trail - it was a little difficult on the second part of the trail but the view was worth it
Easy walk, super view
The views are fantastic. Be sure to bring proper footwear as there are tons of rocks and tree roots. Would definitely recommend!
Great and fun hike

The hike is a bit hard, lots of rocks and was a bit slippery because of rain. But it was very adventurous and different! The view from top is Extraordinary! 
It’s dangerous though. If you have kids this trail is hard on them.
Very very slippery. It rained pretty much the whole time when I went
Beautiful hike

I noticed a lot of trash along the trail and cliffside, including empty bottles, beer cans, and tissues. Please make sure to take your trash with you when you leave—if you brought it with you, please take it back. It would be great if everyone could pitch in to keep the area clean and enjoyable for all. Thanks for being respectful and helping out!
Great hike with fantastic views. There is a sign at the actual lookout so make sure you go all the way. There's also a cool hole in the rocks just past the actual lookout that is worth seeing.
Beautiful hike... A bit muddy and slippery

It poured here most of the afternoon. Rain stopped at 4 so we headed off,  a little muddy. Definitely need a good pair of hiking boots but sneakers would do. Lot of tree tops and rock to walk over.   Views are amazing.
Don’t wear white shoes. Highly recommend hiking boots. But beautiful and amazing.
Amazing trail with so many lookouts! But make sure you get to the top for the incredible view. The trail was muddy after a rainy morning, so good running/hiking shoes recommended.

Its a difficult terrain, consider bringing proper hiking shoes. The view at the top is fantastic, keep following the guided trail till you reach a wide area with a proper view of the rock formations and cliffs.
Amazing hike. Sat on the lions head
Quick trail for a nice view at the end!
Awesome
Lovely out and back trail!

Great trail. It took us about 2 hours round trip to the lookout and back. It is a moderate to difficult trail so wear hiking boots or good runners. We saw people in dresses and flip-flops and suspect they were a but muddy and sore afterwards.
Trail is well marked. Lookout view is beautiful. Not too much mosquitoes today. Recommend to wear hiking shoes.
very rugged trail , marked super clear ! Definitely worth the trip !
lots of rocks

Make sure you book parking in advance. Small parking lot that needs pre-paid reservation. $20 for 4 hours, which is more than enough time at a good walking pace. Trail is well marked and heavily used so it's difficult to get lost. The trail is mostly rocky so wear sturdy shoes. Beautiful lookouts over Georgian Bay. Definitely worth the time and energy. No bugs.

amazing trail, amazing views
100% worth it

We took our 3 kids (6,10,12) and it was a good challenge for them.  It took 1.5 hours out and 1 hour 10 min back. Saw lots of people wearing sandals and new shoes and expect they will be turning around.  You need runners or hiking shoes/boots for this hike when the conditions are wet and muddy.  The lookouts having amazing views.  Worth the hike.

Took just over an hour to get to lions head Lookout. The trail was quite busy on a weekend. We also took the shuttle from the arena. Went past the Lookout to McKay's Harbour which was another 2km or so. We swam for a bit here and then hiked back. Trail is quite rocky. beautiful views
Fun hikes and great views. Very busy
Great hike with amazing views. Would love to explore more some day. Difficult terrain with lots of rocks and roots. A little muddy today. go a little to the east of the lookout to see the keyhole.

Went on a Tuesday, and the parking lot was less than half full. Nice wide trail with clear markings. Thanks to the sun over the weekend, the trail wasn’t slushy or muddy since a lot of it dried up. Great views at the top!
Muddy, rocky and quite difficult but beautiful.
Lots of mud and rocks. Hiking shoes advised

This is a beautiful but fairly long and difficult trail. Completely worth the adventure and views. Do plan to get a parking ticket ahead of time as the slots sell out online and might be hard to get a spot.
Very muddy trail so be prepared

Be the first in and out if you want to see the sunrise and avoid the traffic and reservations. 
 Hike with headlamps and trail shoes/boots
Am tired

Fun out & back hike with beautiful bay views! The kids enjoyed scrambling up in to the pothole - so neat!  Some muddy spots but nothing too terrible - wear proper shoes to help navigate the rocky terrain. Be sure to check out the keyhole, which is just past the Lion’s Head Lookout - follow the trail down a  steep but short hill and it can be found on the bay side.
Pretty muddy today. Lots of climbing over and on rocks and roots but worth it for the great views at the top.

Well marked trail. The expected mud was there post rain, so I’m glad we wore proper shoes because we were all sporting a fair bit of mud by the end. Most of the trail is quite rocky (limestone outcroppings) so paying attention to foot placement is important. I hope the fellow explorers we encountered on our walk out didn’t ruin their new white shoes and flip-flops in the mud.

My crew and I filled a grocery bag with garbage on our way out as our good deed for the day. (Beer cans, plastic water bottles and candy wrappers discarded here and there.)

Remember to pack out what you bring in everyone. Let’s keep the trail beautiful.
Rainy day, not recommended.
wear good shoes. The trail is not difficult but the footing is uneven most of the way.

I’d say it’s an easy trail for the average person. Gets a little bit rocky and slightly steep at the very end but overall very enjoyable and easy walk!! Need to book parking in advance as we had to park 20 min down the road and walk up which wasn’t bad at all! AMAZING views, best hike i’ve done in Ontario!!
We completed this in record time.  We had 6:30-10:30 reserved parking.    We showed up at 8:45(overslept).   We hustled and only spent 5 minutes kat lions head but it can be done.

Just amazing, 
Don’t forget to bring enough water.
Must wear hiking shoes  and  spray

Beautiful day for a hike. Trail mostly protected from the sun. Occasionally buggy and muddy. Stunning views. Need to be very careful at the cliffs’ edge. Took us 3 hours but went beyond the lookout and stopped often for photos.
Some muddy spots, some rocky spots very well-marked trail. Lovely view from the lookout.

Consider booking time slot for parking early. $20 for parking. Arrive early to this trail as it gets extremely busy. Trail is well groomed, lots of rock bed and some muddy spots but not bad. The lookout was incredibly beautiful.

Absolutely beautiful views! Some rocky sections but nothing crazy. It was muddy today but nothing hiking boots can’t handle. I didn’t notice any bugs which was great. Far too peopley for my liking. Lots of litter which is so upsetting. Small parking lot with paid parking online.
Some parts are difficult. Good running shoes are recommended.
Beautiful hike (forgot to end trail was about 3 hours a trek) pretty rocky but so worth it for the views! 10/10 recommended

Worth it! Beautiful view. But please do not litter. Found empty packets, cans and empty plastic bottles along the way. Be mindful and take your garbage with you. Also view points are not private property. Please do not use them as your picnic spot and make others uncomfortable. Please let everyone enjoy the view.
Parked at the arena and walked up to the trailhead. Incredible trail, we had an amazing time. It was quite busy but still extremely worth the hike!
Wear proper hiking shoes.
Make sure you go till the Lion’s Head Point (it is about 500-600 m from the Lion’s Head Lookout), that’s where you can see the Lion’s head forming from the rock. It’s beautiful!!
Beautiful trail, well maintained, and the look out was spectacular. Not too busy either.
All about the views absolutely worth a later evening hike! Albeit 2 Scot’s being pretty scared of potential Black Bears round each corner!!
Amazing. Bout 3-3.5 return hike

Beautiful trail, very muddy due to recent rainfall. 

There is a lot of litter on the trail, if you’re hiking please pack in, pack out!!

Note that the Bruce Trail Moore Street Side Trail was recently closed by the Bruce Trail Conservancy, at the request of the landowners, due to trail degradation and environmental damage. Access to the Lion's Head Lookout is only available from the main trail entrance at the McCurdy parking lot or at the end of Cemetery Road (and currently numbers aren't monitored even though the trail is generally at over capacity during good weather days). The McCurdy parking lot is a small parking lot, with 4 porte-potties and trash/recycle bins, but no other facilities. Overflow parking is available at the Lion's Head Arena (near the LCBO on Ferndale Road) and just walk the 1 km back to the McCurdy main trail entrance. As of August 2020, no parking is permitted on Moore St. (from hospital to the end of the road). In addition, if you are using Google/GPS to get to this destination, the directions that take you to the end of Moore St. with access to the Lookout are INCORRECT. This is a residential area and all property is private, therefore no trespassing - use the main trail. Littering and trail degradation is a real problem in this Nature Preserve - so please do your part - even consider finding another trail in the area to reduce the over-use.
